brief.subject: FTC: Imposter scams still the top reported fraud
brief.headline: FTC Removes 19 Fake FTC Websites as Imposter Scams Lead Fraud Reports
brief.dek: The FTC reports progress against impersonators, warns health plan marketers during open enrollment, and targets hidden business fees.
brief.lede: Imposter scams remain the top reported fraud category, and the FTC says it has removed 19 websites pretending to be the agency itself.

sections.heading: Fake FTC websites pulled offline
bullets: 19 websites posing as the FTC have been taken down, proving scammers will even impersonate fraud fighters.
More than $80 million in consumer redress has come from enforcement since the Impersonation Rule took effect in 2024.
Imposter scams lead all reported fraud, so treat unexpected contacts claiming government authority with suspicion.

sections.heading: Open enrollment: watch health plan pitches
bullets: 25 companies selling or generating leads for health plans received FTC warning letters during open enrollment.
The letters flag deceptive or unfair claims about plan terms that likely break laws the agency enforces.
More letters will follow on a rolling basis, so confirm coverage details before signing up.

sections.heading: Small businesses hit by hidden fees
bullets: $600,000 settlement: Riverside Payments and an affiliate allegedly promised savings and blocked 'risk-free' cancellations.
The FTC and several states sued Toast Inc., alleging hidden fees and deceptive subscription and cancellation practices aimed at restaurants.
Small business owners should review processing contracts for cancellation terms and unexpected charges.

brief.seo_description: FTC removes 19 fake FTC websites, warns 25 health plan marketers during open enrollment, and acts on hidden fees aimed at small businesses.
